title: Appkin configuration v3
description: Machine-readable contract for an Appkin v3 application. schemaVersion is optional for backward compatibility; new configurations should set it to 3.

schemaVersion.description: Configuration-language version. Optional only for compatibility with configurations created before schema versioning was introduced.

icon.description: One emoji for the app's icon on the home page and the phone's home screen, such as "🏍️". Without it, the icon is the name's first letter.

views.description: Reusable view definitions. References are not valid in this registry.

actions.description: Reusable action definitions. References are not valid in this registry.

data.description: Arbitrary JSON object made available to mappings and interpolation.

headers.description: Request headers, such as { "Authorization": "Bearer __API_TOKEN__" }. Values may use ${field} placeholders and __NAME__ API-key placeholders. Appkin sets User-Agent, Host, Content-Type and Content-Length itself.

visibleIf.description: A path in the view's data, such as creators or current_location: the view is shown only when there is a value there that isn't null, empty, false, 0 or an empty array. Start it with ! to show the view only when there isn't. Only presence tests, no expressions.

view.description: A view definition (it has a type), an explicit reference (ref) or a legacy ID-only reference.

explicitViewReference.title: Explicit view reference (preferred)
explicitViewReference.description: References a reusable root view by ID. New configurations should use this unambiguous form.

legacyViewReference.title: Legacy view reference
legacyViewReference.description: Backward-compatible ID-only reference. Prefer the explicit ref property in new configurations.

viewDefinition.description: A view, chosen by its type: only that type's rules apply, so a mistake is reported once.

orientation.description: How the child views are arranged; vertical by default

mapping.description: Path of a value in the current data to show as the text, such as owner.name

title.description: The text, when no mapping value is shown

label.description: First line of the text view, shown above the text

labelStyle.description: The label's own style, so a bold heading needn't make its text bold; without it the label looks like the text

format.description:
plain (default); html: simple HTML in the text (``, ``, ``, ``, ``, `
`, `

`, ``), such as a museum's descriptions; or markdown: headings (`#`), `**bold**`, `*italics*`, lists (`-` or `1.`), quotes (`>`), `` `code` `` and `[links](https://...)`, such as a description you write

showWhenEmpty.description: Show the label even when the mapping or title has nothing to show. By default such a text view isn't drawn at all.

checkView.description: A tick box, ticked when the data's true/false value at mapping is true. Ticking the box runs its action at once with that value turned over, so an update event saves it; a ticked title is struck through. Only the box ticks: a tap on the title reaches the list item.

action.description: Runs when the box is ticked or unticked, with the data where the value at mapping says so; usually an update event

mapping.description: The field holding true or false, such as "done"

title.description: The text beside the box; may use ${field} placeholders

mapping.description: Path of a value in the current data to use as the button's text

label.description: Not displayed on buttons: use title. On a button with only an icon, what screen readers say, such as "Delete ${title}"

icon.description: An icon from the phone's standard set, before the title; without a title the button is just the icon, in its own small size

mapping.description: Path of an image address in the current data

scale.description: crop (default): the picture fills its space and its edges may be cut; fit: the whole picture shows, inside its space

action.description: What tapping an item does; its event receives that item

swipeToStart.description: What swiping an item towards the start (left) does; its event receives that item, such as an alert asking before a delete. The item slides back unless the action removes it

swipeToStartIcon.description: The icon under an item swiped towards the start; delete by default

swipeToEnd.description: What swiping an item towards the end (right) does; its event receives that item, such as an update marking it done

swipeToEndIcon.description: The icon under an item swiped towards the end; check by default

mapping.description: Path of the array of objects to show, in data or in the initData response

itemView.description: The view repeated for each item; its mappings and placeholders refer to that item

initData.description: A REST request whose JSON response is the list's data

stored.description: Shows objects the app saved on the phone with a save event, instead of initData or data; mapping is not used

orientation.description: vertical (default): one item per row; horizontal: a row that scrolls sideways; grid: items side by side in rows of columns

columns.description: Items per row of a grid; 2 by default

emptyText.description: What the list says when it has no items, instead of No data available; may use ${field} placeholders

storedSort.description: By the field by; values listed in order come first, in that order (such as ["High", "Medium", "Low"]), then the others, numbers by size and text alphabetically. Objects without the field come last; ties keep the order they were saved in.

by.description: The field to sort by, such as "priority"

order.description: Values in the order they come first, always as text, also for numbers and true/false (such as ["false", "true"])

storedData.description: The objects a save event put in a collection, oldest first; it shows them again when that collection changes.

collection.description: The collection's name, as in the save event

where.description: Only the objects whose fields have these values; values may use ${field} placeholders from the list's data, such as { "appId": "${id}" }

sort.description: The order: one sort, or a list where each later sort orders what the earlier ones leave tied (such as done last, then by priority)

sortOptions.description: Orders the user can choose, as a row of buttons above the list (the first until they choose); they replace sort. Keep titles short, such as Status, Priority, Newest

filterBy.description: A field of tags (a tags field's list, or text with commas): the list offers a chip per tag in use, after All, to show only items with that tag

initialItems.description: Objects saved in the collection the first time the list opens, when nothing was ever saved there: a checklist to tick off (places to visit, things to pack), whose items update and delete then change like any saved object. Give each a key field and set unique so a later version's new items are added too

unique.description: A field of initialItems that tells them apart, such as "key": each time the list opens, the initial items whose value there was never added are saved (a later version's new places); the ones already saved stay as the user left them, and deleted ones don't come back

action.description: Runs on submit, with the submitted object as data

buttonTitle.description: The submit button's text; Submit by default

formElements.description: The fields; each one puts its value under its mapping in the submitted object

formElement.description: A form field, chosen by its type.

mapping.description: Key of the submitted object that receives the value

mandatory.description: Must be filled in before submitting

multiline.description: Takes several lines (Enter starts a new one), growing as it fills: for notes and descriptions

options.description: The choices: each is a string, shown and submitted, or { "label": shown, "value": submitted }, such as { "label": "Any type", "value": "" }

label.description: What the option shows; its value by default

value.description: What the form submits when it's chosen

dateValue.description: A date string accepted by Jackson or an epoch-millisecond number.

timeInput.description: A time of day, picked on a clock and submitted as HH:mm, as a calendar event's time takes it.

tagsInput.description: Short labels the user adds one by one (Enter adds one), shown as chips; it submits a list of texts, which a stored list's filterBy offers as filter chips.

mandatory.description: At least one tag is needed

photosInput.description: Photos picked from the phone's gallery, kept on the phone with the app. It submits a list of photo references; an image view whose mapping is that list shows them in a row.

mapping.description: Where the list of photos goes, such as "photos"

mandatory.description: At least one photo is needed

max.description: How many photos it takes; 10 by default

hiddenInput.description: A value the form sends without showing it, such as the id of the item on screen.

mapping.description: Key of the submitted object that receives the value

value.description: The value, sent as text; may use ${field} placeholders filled in from the screen's data. Without it, the data's value at mapping is sent.

mapping.description: Key of the submitted object that receives true or false

action.description: An action definition (it has an event), an explicit reference (ref) or a legacy ID-only reference.

explicitActionReference.title: Explicit action reference (preferred)
explicitActionReference.description: References a reusable root action by ID. New configurations should use this unambiguous form.

event.description: An event, chosen by its type.

url.description: HTTPS address; may use ${field} placeholders from the current data

method.description: get (default), post, put or delete; post and put send the current data as a JSON body

thenDo.description: The event to run next, with the JSON response as data

onError.description: The event to run when the request fails, instead of an alert; its data is the request's, plus error.message and, for an HTTP error, error.status

method.description: get (default), post, put or delete; post and put send the current data as a JSON body

nextPage.description: How the list asks for more items when it nears its end. Either parameter and step: that query parameter (such as skip) grows by step, the page size, until a page has fewer items. Or urlFrom: the path in the response of the next page's URL, until there is none.

parameter.description: The query parameter that says where a page starts, such as skip or offset

step.description: How much it grows from page to page: the page size

urlFrom.description: Path in each response of the next page's URL, such as info.next

view.description: The view to open; it receives the current data

mapping.description: Path of the part of the current data the view receives

title.description: The opened screen's title in the app bar, instead of the app's name; may use ${field} placeholders from the data it receives

calendarEvent.description: Opens the phone's calendar app on a new event, filled in; the user reviews and saves it there.

title.description: The event's title; may use ${field} placeholders

date.description: The day, dd/MM/yyyy; may be a placeholder such as ${date} from a form's date field

time.description: The start time, HH:mm; without it the event lasts all day

durationMinutes.description: How long a timed event lasts; 60 by default

location.description: Where it happens; may use ${field} placeholders

description.description: Notes for the event; may use ${field} placeholders

copyEvent.description: Copies a text to the clipboard, to paste anywhere (a chat, a note); the phone confirms it.

text.description: What is copied; may use ${field} placeholders, and a line whose placeholders all have no value is left out, such as "${title}\n${description}"

mapping.description: Path of the part of the current data the text is filled in from

pdfEvent.description: Makes a PDF of saved objects, such as the ideas not done yet: a title, then each object's text as Markdown with its photos below. The share sheet opens on the PDF, to send, save or print it.

collection.description: The collection whose objects it shows

where.description: Only the objects whose fields have these values; values may use ${field} placeholders from the current data, such as { "appId": "${id}", "done": false }

sort.description: The order, as a stored list's sort

title.description: The heading at the top and the file's name; may use ${field} placeholders from the current data. The app's name by default

text.description: Each object's part, as Markdown with ${field} placeholders from the object, such as "## ${title}\n${description}"; a line whose placeholders all have no value is left out

photos.description: Path of each object's photos (a photos field's list) to show below its text

emptyText.description: What an alert says when no object matches, instead of an empty PDF; may use ${field} placeholders

pageless.description: true: one page as tall as everything, best read on a phone; false (default): A4 pages, for printing

mapping.description: Path of the part of the current data to use

backEvent.description: Closes the current screen and goes back to the one that opened it, as the phone's Back does; such as after saving an edit.

updateEvent.description: Changes a saved object: the current data (a form's submitted values, or a ticked check's item) and fields replace its values; a form's field left empty is removed from it. Its id and createdAt never change.

collection.description: The collection the object is in

id.description: The id of the object to change; "${id}" (the current data's id) by default

fields.description: Values to set too; text may use ${field} placeholders, filled as in a save event

thenDo.description: The event to run next, with the changed object as data

mapping.description: Path of the part of the current data to save

deleteEvent.description: Removes saved objects: the one whose id is id (the current data's by default), or every one where matches. Put it behind an alert's thenDoOK to ask first.

id.description: The id of the object to remove; "${id}" (the current data's id) by default

where.description: Instead of id: removes every object whose fields have these values, with ${field} placeholders from the current data, such as { "appId": "${id}" }

thenDo.description: The event to run next, with the current data

mapping.description: Path of the part of the current data the id or where is filled in from

saveEvent.description: Saves the current data (a form's submitted values) on the phone as a new object of a collection; a list with stored shows the collection. Each object gets an id and createdAt (epoch milliseconds). A form saved this way starts empty, not filled in from the screen's data (only its hidden fields take that, such as an app's id), and empty again after each save.

collection.description: The collection to add to, such as "ideas"; each app has its own

fields.description: Values to add to the object; text may use ${field} placeholders from the data the form showed (the screen's, or a list row's), then from the submitted values, such as { "appId": "${id}" }

unique.description: A field that tells saved objects apart, such as "key": saving an object with the same value there replaces the one already saved (keeping its id) instead of adding another

thenDo.description: The event to run next, with the saved object as data

mapping.description: Path of the part of the current data to save

openEvent.description: Hands an address to another app on the phone: https or http opens the browser, geo: a map, tel: the dialer (nothing is called) and mailto: an email app. No other kinds of address are opened.

url.description: An https:, http:, geo:, tel: or mailto: address, or a placeholder holding one, such as ${url}; values placeholders insert are percent-encoded

mapping.description: Path of the part of the current data the address is filled in from

shareEvent.description: Opens the phone's share sheet on a text, for the user to send to any app.

text.description: What is shared; may use ${field} placeholders, such as "${title} ${url}"; a line whose placeholders all have no value is left out

photos.description: Path of the photos to share with the text, such as "photos" (a photos field's list): they go as attachments, the text as their caption

mapping.description: Path of the part of the current data the text is filled in from

thenDoOK.description: The event to run when OK is tapped

thenDoKO.description: The event to run when the alert is cancelled
